original_question: For the families of Welch W1 and Golomb G2 Costas arrays, determine the maximal pairwise cross-correlation quantities defined by the paper as Ψ_W1(p) and Ψ_G2(q), classify primes and prime powers into the cases stated in Problem 21, prove the listed formulas and exceptional cases, derive formulas for the local minima, and show where the maxima are attained in the non-safe cases described there.
target_in_paper: Section 7.4, Problem 21, “Cross-correlation of G2 and W1 arrays,” on pages 15–16. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
correct_elements: Your draft is aimed at the correct target: Problem 21 explicitly defines the maximal cross-correlation quantities Ψ_W1(p) and Ψ_G2(q), asks for the prime and prime-power case splits, includes the exceptional cases p=19 and q=16, asks for formulas for the local minima, and asks for proofs that the maxima are attained at (0,0) in the specified non-safe cases. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
missing_details: A stand-alone version must define the cross-correlation operator exactly: for f,g:[n]→[n] and (u,v)∈Z^2, Ψ_{f,g}(u,v)=|{(f(i)+v,i+u):i∈[n]}∩{(g(i),i):i∈[n]}|, with ordinary integer addition, not modular addition. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

It must define the Welch family W1 precisely from Theorem 1: exponential Welch permutations f:[p−1]→[p−1], f(i)=α^(i−1+c) mod p, where α is a primitive root of F(p) and c∈[p−1]−1, together with their logarithmic inverses, since the surrounding text says these together form W1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

It must define the Golomb family G2 precisely from Theorem 3: for q=p^m and primitive roots α,β of F(q), the permutation f:[q−2]→[q−2] is characterized by α^(f(i))+β^i=1. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
The draft should state the orders of the arrays being compared: W1 arrays have order p−1, while G2 arrays have order q−2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

For Ψ_W1(p), the inner maximum is not merely over distinct permutations; the paper writes max over f1^pr≠f2, meaning the two W1 permutations must be generated by different primitive roots. For Ψ_G2(q), the inner maximum is over distinct G2 permutations f′1≠f′2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

The prime classification is specifically with respect to the pair of quantities Ψ_W1(p) and Ψ_G2(p), and the first case uses t equal to the smallest prime satisfying p≡1 mod (2t). The exceptional prime p=19 must be named explicitly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

The prime-power classification is specifically with respect to Ψ_G2(q): one must state the three cases exactly, including q≠16 in the generic case, the even/odd split in the definition of t, the exceptional value q=16, and the two local-minimum subcases ‘(q−1)/2 prime’ and ‘q−1 prime’. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

Because the paper declares that primes are included among prime powers unless explicitly excluded, the final origin-attainment clause for G2 must be read with q possibly prime; this is why the paper excludes q=16,19 there. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

A fully faithful stand-alone version should note the apparent typographical inconsistency in the first prime-power bullet: the paper prints Ψ_W1(q), but the sentence introducing that bullet and the surrounding bullets make clear that the intended quantity is Ψ_G2(q). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))

Likewise, the last sentence’s explicit parameter formula for the G2 pair is internally awkward as printed; to make the question usable, one should specify that the second G2 permutation is generated from (α^r,β), with r chosen as in the final sentence of Problem 21, while noting that the printed line appears to contain a variable inconsistency. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
refined_question: Let p be a prime and q a prime power, with primes counted among prime powers as in the paper. Let W1 be the Welch family from Theorem 1: exponential Welch permutations f:[p−1]→[p−1], f(i)=α^(i−1+c) mod p, where α is a primitive root of F(p) and c∈[p−1]−1, together with their logarithmic inverses; and let G2 be the Golomb family from Theorem 3: for q=p^m and primitive roots α,β∈F(q), the permutation f:[q−2]→[q−2] determined by α^(f(i))+β^i=1. For permutations f,g:[n]→[n], define Ψ_{f,g}(u,v)=|{(f(i)+v,i+u):i∈[n]}∩{(g(i),i):i∈[n]}| for (u,v)∈Z^2. Define Ψ_W1(p)=max_{(u,v)∈Z^2} max_{f1^pr≠f2} Ψ_{f1,f2}(u,v), where f1,f2 are W1 permutations of order p−1 and f1^pr≠f2 means that they are generated by different primitive roots, and define Ψ_G2(q)=max_{(u,v)∈Z^2} max_{f′1≠f′2} Ψ_{f′1,f′2}(u,v), where f′1,f′2 are distinct G2 permutations of order q−2. Prove the exact trichotomy stated in Problem 21: (1) with respect to Ψ_W1(p) and Ψ_G2(p), if p is a non-safe prime with p≠19, then Ψ_W1(p)=Ψ_G2(p)+1=(p−1)/t, where t is the smallest prime such that p≡1 mod (2t); if p=19, then Ψ_W1(19)=Ψ_G2(19)=6=(19−1)/3; and if (p−1)/2 is prime, then p is a local minimum of both Ψ_W1 and Ψ_G2; (2) with respect to Ψ_G2(q), if q≠16 and neither (q−1)/2 nor q−1 is prime, then Ψ_G2(q)=(q−1)/t−1, where t is the smallest prime such that q≡1 mod (2t) when q is odd, or q≡1 mod t when q is even; if q=16, then Ψ_G2(16)=5=(16−1)/3; and if either (q−1)/2 is prime or q−1 is prime, then q is a local minimum of Ψ_G2; derive formulas for the values of these local minima in both the prime and prime-power settings; and finally prove the paper’s origin-attainment statements, namely that for every non-safe prime p, Ψ_W1(p)=max_{f1^pr≠f2} Ψ_{f1,f2}(0,0), and that for every non-safe prime power q≠16,19 with q−1 not prime, Ψ_G2(q)=Ψ_{f′1,f′2}(0,0) for a pair of G2 permutations f′1,f′2 generated from (α,β) and (α^r,β), with r chosen as in the final sentence of Problem 21. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation in the paper. Section 7.4 sets up the cross-correlation context, and Problem 21 then states, almost verbatim, the program your draft is aiming at: define Ψ_W1 and Ψ_G2, classify primes and prime powers into three cases, isolate the exceptional values p=19 and q=16, derive formulas for the local minima, and show that in the specified non-safe cases the maximal value is achieved at the origin. To make the question genuinely stand-alone, one must import the notation from Definition 2 and the family definitions from Theorems 1 and 3. I also regularized the first prime-power bullet to Ψ_G2(q), because the printed Ψ_W1(q) is inconsistent with the sentence immediately introducing that part of the problem and with the rest of the bullet list. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1102.5727))
